title: Cold email to a senior alumna at Razorpay
persona: Nivedita, 3rd-year, looking for a product internship
scenario: You found an alumna 5 years out of college, now PM at Razorpay. You want a 15-min coffee chat about breaking into product. She gets ~10 cold emails a week. You want one that's short, names a specific thing she shipped (so it's clear you actually looked her up), asks one specific question (not ‘any advice’), proposes 3 time slots, and doesn't end with ‘any time that works for you’. No ‘I hope this email finds you well’.
badPrompt: write a cold email to a senior alumna asking for advice about product management
badOutput:
Dear [Name],

I hope this email finds you well. I am a 3rd-year student passionate about product management. I came across your profile and was very inspired by your journey. Would you be open to a quick chat at your convenience? Any advice would be greatly appreciated.

Warm regards,
Nivedita

hints.title: Force a specific reference
hints.body: ‘Name something specific she shipped or wrote about.’ Without this, your email is one of 10 generic ones that week.

hints.title: Ban the corporate-grovel openers
hints.body: ‘No ‘hope this email finds you well’, no ‘inspired by your journey’, no ‘any advice’.’ Senior PMs read these and delete.

checks.tip: Frame the artifact, a cold email.
Anchor the recipient, senior alumna PM at Razorpay.
Reference her inbox volume, ~10 cold emails a week.
Anchor your context, 3rd-year looking for a product internship.
Force a specific reference to something she shipped/wrote.
Force one specific question, not ‘any advice’.
Demand 3 specific time slots, not ‘any time that works for you’.
Specify a subject line that doesn't read as cold spam.

tipIfLow: Cold emails fail when they're generic. The unlock is naming a specific thing she shipped, asking ONE specific question (not ‘any advice’), proposing 3 time slots (not ‘any time that works for you’). Specificity is respect for her inbox.
goldPrompt: Act as someone who reads 10 cold emails a week and deletes 9. I'm Nivedita, 3rd-year, want a 15-min coffee chat with a Razorpay PM 5 years out (alumna). Banned openers: 'hope this finds you well', 'inspired by your journey', 'any advice'. The email must, in under 120 words: (1) name ONE specific thing she shipped or wrote about (you'll ask me what), (2) ask ONE specific question about that thing — not 'how do I break into product', (3) propose 3 concrete time slots, (4) close with a specific next-step ask, NOT 'any time that works'. Subject line ≤ 8 words.
